questions.q: The change of a gas into a liquid is called
questions.explanation: On cooling, gas particles lose energy and come together to form a liquid, which is condensation.

questions.q: The change of a solid into a liquid at its melting point is called
questions.explanation: Melting is also called fusion.

questions.q: Which of the following is a property of solids?
options: They take the shape of their container
They can be compressed a great deal
They have a fixed shape and negligible compressibility
questions.explanation: Solid particles are held in fixed positions, so a solid keeps its shape and is hard to compress.

questions.q: Gases can be turned into liquids by
options: applying pressure and lowering the temperature
questions.explanation: Pressure and cooling push the particles close together so they form a liquid.

questions.q: Acetone evaporates faster than water at the same temperature because
options: the forces of attraction between its particles are weaker
questions.explanation: Weaker attractions let particles escape easily; acetone boils at a lower temperature than water.

questions.q: Food cooks faster in a pressure cooker because
options: water boils at a lower temperature inside it
the increased pressure raises the boiling point, so the food is heated to a higher temperature
questions.explanation: Higher pressure raises the boiling point of water, so the contents become hotter than 100 °C.

questions.q: Ice at 0 °C cools a drink better than the same mass of water at 0 °C because the ice
options: absorbs extra heat (latent heat of fusion) in order to melt
questions.explanation: Melting ice takes in the latent heat of fusion from the drink.

questions.q: Why does a gas exert pressure on the walls of its container?
questions.answer: The particles of a gas move randomly at high speed and keep colliding with the walls of the container. The force of these collisions per unit area is the gas pressure.
keyPoints: Gas particles move randomly at high speed
Force per unit area is pressure
questions.explanation: More frequent or harder collisions mean higher pressure.

questions.q: Describe an activity to show that particles of matter are very small.
questions.answer: Dissolve two or three crystals of potassium permanganate in a glass of water and note the colour. Take a small amount of this solution and dilute it again and again with water. Even after many dilutions the water is still slightly coloured, which shows that a few crystals contain a huge number of tiny particles.
keyPoints: Dissolve a few crystals in water
questions.explanation: A visible colour after huge dilution means a tiny crystal contains a very large number of particles.

questions.q: Which of the following is a suspension?
questions.explanation: In muddy water the solid particles are large and settle when left undisturbed.

questions.q: Which of the following is a compound?
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide is made of carbon and oxygen chemically combined.

questions.q: An alloy is
options: a homogeneous mixture of metals, or of a metal and a non-metal
a suspension of a metal in water
questions.explanation: Alloys such as brass and steel are homogeneous mixtures.

questions.q: A saturated solution is one in which
options: more solute can easily be added
no more solute can dissolve at that temperature
the solute is always a gas
questions.explanation: A saturated solution already holds the maximum amount of solute at that temperature.

questions.q: Cream is separated from milk by
questions.explanation: Spinning the milk quickly throws the denser parts outward and the lighter cream stays on top.

questions.q: Sugar cannot be separated from its aqueous solution by filtration because
options: the dissolved particles are smaller than the pores of the filter paper
questions.explanation: Dissolved particles are extremely small and pass through the filter paper.

questions.q: When iron filings and sulphur are heated together, a black solid is formed which is not attracted by a magnet. This is a compound because it
options: is attracted by a magnet like iron
has a fixed composition and properties different from iron and sulphur
can be separated by a magnet
is still just a mixture of the two
questions.explanation: A new substance with different properties shows that a chemical combination has taken place.

questions.q: What is the Tyndall effect? Why does it not occur in a true solution?
questions.answer: The Tyndall effect is the scattering of a beam of light by particles of a colloid or suspension, which makes the path of the beam visible. In a true solution the particles are too small to scatter light, so the beam is not visible.
questions.explanation: Only particles of larger size scatter light noticeably.

questions.q: How can pure water be obtained from salt water? State the principle.
questions.answer: Salt water is heated in a distillation flask. The water evaporates, the vapour passes into a condenser where it cools back into liquid water, and the salt is left in the flask. The principle is that water and salt differ greatly in volatility.
keyPoints: Water vapour condensed in a condenser
questions.explanation: Only the volatile component, water, leaves the flask.

questions.q: The chemical symbol of iron is
questions.explanation: Fe comes from the Latin name ferrum.

questions.q: The chemical symbol of potassium is
questions.explanation: K comes from the Latin name kalium.

questions.q: The value of the Avogadro constant is
questions.explanation: One mole of any substance contains 6.022 × 10^23 particles.

questions.q: The molecular mass of water (H = 1 u, O = 16 u) is
How many moles are there in 36 g of water? (molar mass 18 g/mol)
One mole of nitrogen gas, N2, contains how many moles of nitrogen atoms?
questions.explanation: Each N2 molecule has two atoms, so one mole of molecules has 2 moles of atoms.

questions.q: What is the mass of 3 moles of ammonia, NH3? (N = 14 u, H = 1 u)
questions.explanation: Molar mass = 14 + 3 = 17 g/mol, so 3 × 17 = 51 g.

questions.q: What is a mole? How is it related to the Avogadro constant?
questions.answer: A mole is the amount of a substance that contains 6.022 × 10^23 particles (atoms, molecules or ions) of it. This number is the Avogadro constant, and one mole of a substance has a mass equal to its atomic or molecular mass in grams.
keyPoints: That number is the Avogadro constant
Mass of one mole is molar mass in grams
questions.explanation: The mole links the number of particles to measurable mass.

questions.q: 3 g of carbon combines with 8 g of oxygen to form carbon dioxide. How much oxygen is needed to burn 9 g of carbon completely to carbon dioxide? Which law do you use?
questions.answer: The ratio of carbon to oxygen by mass in carbon dioxide is fixed at 3 : 8. So 9 g of carbon needs 8 × 3 = 24 g of oxygen. This uses the law of constant proportions.
questions.explanation: A pure compound always has the same elements in the same mass ratio.

questions.q: Atoms of the same element that have different mass numbers are called
questions.explanation: Isotopes have the same atomic number but different numbers of neutrons.

questions.q: Which particle is present in the nucleus of an atom?
questions.explanation: The nucleus contains protons and neutrons.

questions.q: The plum-pudding model of the atom was proposed by
questions.explanation: Thomson pictured electrons embedded in a positively charged sphere.

questions.q: In Rutherford's experiment most alpha particles passed straight through the gold foil. This showed that
options: most of the space inside an atom is empty
the atom is a solid sphere
electrons are heavier than alpha particles
questions.explanation: Particles went through undeflected because most of the atom is empty space.

questions.q: How many electrons does a sodium ion, Na+, have? (atomic number of sodium = 11)
questions.explanation: The atom has 11 electrons and Na+ has lost one, leaving 10.

questions.q: The valency of oxygen (electronic configuration 2, 6) is
questions.explanation: Oxygen needs two more electrons to complete its octet, so its valency is 2.

questions.q: An element has the electronic configuration 2, 8, 3. Its atomic number is
questions.explanation: The atom has 2 + 8 + 3 = 13 electrons, so its atomic number is 13.

questions.q: Differentiate between isotopes and isobars with one example of each.
questions.answer: Isotopes are atoms of the same element with the same atomic number but different mass numbers, for example carbon-12 and carbon-14. Isobars are atoms of different elements with the same mass number but different atomic numbers, for example argon-40 and calcium-40.
keyPoints: Isotopes: same atomic number, different mass number
Isobars: same mass number, different atomic number
questions.explanation: The terms compare the atomic number and the mass number.

questions.q: An atom X has 19 protons and 20 neutrons. Give its atomic number, mass number, electronic configuration and valency.
questions.answer: Atomic number = 19, mass number = 19 + 20 = 39. The electronic configuration is 2, 8, 8, 1. It has one electron in its outermost shell, so its valency is 1.
questions.explanation: The number of protons fixes the electrons of a neutral atom.

questions.q: The smallest structural and functional unit of living organisms is the
questions.explanation: All living organisms are made of cells.

questions.q: The jelly-like substance that fills the region between the nucleus and the plasma membrane is the
questions.explanation: Cytoplasm holds the cell organelles.

questions.q: Plastids are found in
questions.explanation: Plastids such as chloroplasts occur in plant cells.

questions.q: Oxygen enters a cell by moving from a region of higher concentration to one of lower concentration. This process is
questions.explanation: Movement of a substance from high to low concentration is diffusion; osmosis refers only to water.

questions.q: An amoeba takes in food by engulfing it with its flexible plasma membrane. This process is called
questions.explanation: Endocytosis is the taking in of materials by the cell membrane folding around them.

questions.q: The organelle that helps in making fats and removing poisons and drugs in liver cells is the
questions.explanation: Smooth ER is involved in lipid synthesis and detoxification.

questions.q: Which statement forms part of the cell theory?
options: Cells arise spontaneously from non-living matter
Only plants are made of cells
All living things are made of cells and new cells arise from pre-existing cells
Cells are not found in animals
questions.explanation: The cell theory says the cell is the basic unit of life and arises from existing cells.

questions.q: Write two differences between a plant cell and an animal cell.
questions.answer: A plant cell has a cell wall outside the plasma membrane, but an animal cell does not. A plant cell has plastids and a large central vacuole, while an animal cell has no plastids and only small vacuoles.
keyPoints: Cell wall only in plant cells
questions.explanation: These differences are linked to the plant's way of making its own food and keeping its shape.

questions.q: What would happen if the plasma membrane of a cell were ruptured?
questions.answer: The cell contents would leak out and the cell could no longer control which substances enter or leave. The internal environment of the cell would be lost and the cell would die.
keyPoints: Control over entry and exit is lost
questions.explanation: The membrane keeps the cell contents separate from the outside.

questions.q: Contraction and relaxation to bring about movement is the function of
questions.explanation: Muscles shorten and relax to move the body.

questions.q: Meristematic tissue is made of
questions.explanation: Meristematic cells divide to make new cells for growth.

questions.q: Apical meristem is found at the
questions.explanation: Apical meristem lies at the growing tips and increases length.

questions.q: Which tissue has dead, thick-walled cells and gives hardness, as in the husk of a coconut?
questions.explanation: Sclerenchyma cells have lignified walls and provide strength.

questions.q: Parenchyma that contains chlorophyll and carries out photosynthesis is called
questions.explanation: Chlorenchyma has chloroplasts.

questions.q: A thin layer of flat cells forms the lining of the blood vessels and the air sacs of the lungs. This is
questions.explanation: Flat squamous cells allow easy exchange of substances.

questions.q: The cells of cork in the bark of old trees are dead and compactly arranged, with suberin in their walls. This makes the cork
questions.explanation: Suberin makes the cork waterproof, so it protects the plant.

questions.q: Name the four types of animal tissue and give one function of each.
questions.answer: Epithelial tissue covers and protects the body surfaces. Connective tissue joins and supports organs, for example bone or blood. Muscular tissue helps movement. Nervous tissue carries messages as impulses.
questions.explanation: Each tissue is specialised for a different job.

questions.q: How is the structure of a neuron suited to its function?
questions.answer: A neuron has a cell body with a nucleus and long thin extensions. Short branched dendrites receive impulses and a long axon carries the impulse over long distances to other cells, so a neuron can carry messages quickly throughout the body.
questions.explanation: Long extensions let one cell reach far-off parts of the body.

questions.q: A body covers 20 m in 4 s. Its speed is
questions.explanation: Speed = 20 / 4 = 5 m/s.

questions.q: The shortest distance between the initial and the final position of a moving body is its
questions.explanation: Displacement is the shortest distance between the two positions in a given direction.

questions.q: A negative acceleration, in which velocity decreases, is also called
questions.explanation: Retardation or deceleration reduces the velocity of the body.

questions.q: The slope of a velocity-time graph gives
questions.explanation: Change in velocity divided by time is acceleration.

questions.q: A car moves at 36 km/h. Its speed in m/s is
In a distance-time graph, a horizontal straight line parallel to the time axis shows that the body is
questions.explanation: The distance does not change with time, so the body is at rest.

questions.q: A man walks 100 m east and then 40 m west in a straight line. His displacement is
questions.explanation: Net displacement = 100 − 40 = 60 m, towards the east.

questions.q: What is uniform circular motion? Give an example.
questions.answer: Uniform circular motion is motion of a body along a circular path with constant speed. Its velocity changes continuously because its direction keeps changing. An example is the motion of a stone tied to a string whirled in a circle, or the tip of a clock's hand.
keyPoints: Direction, and so velocity, keeps changing
questions.explanation: Although speed is constant the motion is accelerated.

questions.q: A car moving at 20 m/s is brought to rest by brakes giving a retardation of 5 m/s². Find the time taken to stop and the distance covered.
questions.answer: From v = u + at: 0 = 20 − 5t, so t = 4 s. From v² = u² + 2as: 0 = 400 − 10s, so s = 40 m.
keyPoints: Use of equations of motion with a = −5
questions.explanation: Average speed 10 m/s × 4 s also gives 40 m.

questions.q: The force that opposes the relative motion between two surfaces in contact is
questions.explanation: Friction acts opposite to the direction of relative motion.

questions.q: The SI unit of momentum is
questions.explanation: Momentum = mass × velocity, so its unit is kg m/s.

questions.q: Safety belts in cars protect passengers during a sudden stop because of
options: the law of conservation of energy
the inertia of the passengers' bodies (Newton's first law)
questions.explanation: The belt stops the body from continuing forward because of its inertia.

questions.q: What force acts on a 2 kg mass that has an acceleration of 5 m/s²?
A 10 kg body moves at 5 m/s. A 5 kg body has the same momentum. Its velocity is
questions.explanation: Momentum 10 × 5 = 50 kg m/s, so v = 50 / 5 = 10 m/s.

questions.q: A long jumper takes a run before jumping because
options: the inertia of his motion carries him farther
questions.explanation: Inertia of motion adds to the distance of the jump.

questions.q: A constant force of 10 N acts on a 2 kg object initially at rest for 3 s. Its final velocity is
State the law of conservation of momentum.
questions.answer: When two or more objects interact, the total momentum of the objects before the interaction equals the total momentum after it, provided no external unbalanced force acts on them.
questions.explanation: It follows from Newton's second and third laws.

questions.q: Why does a boat move backward when a person jumps forward from it onto the shore?
questions.answer: When the person pushes the boat backward to jump forward, the boat pushes the person forward with an equal and opposite force (third law). The boat gets momentum in the opposite direction, so it moves backward.
keyPoints: Equal and opposite reaction on person
Boat moves backward by conservation of momentum
questions.explanation: Total momentum remains zero, so the two move in opposite directions.

questions.q: The force of attraction between the Earth and an object is called
questions.explanation: The pull of the Earth on objects is the gravitational force.

questions.q: An object that falls under the action of gravity alone is said to be in
questions.explanation: Free fall is motion under gravity with no other force.

questions.q: Pressure is defined as
questions.explanation: Pressure = thrust (force) / area.

questions.q: The SI unit of pressure is the
questions.explanation: One pascal is one newton per square metre.

questions.q: A sharp knife cuts better than a blunt one because the sharp edge
options: has a smaller area, so the same force produces a larger pressure
has a larger area, so there is more pressure
questions.explanation: Pressure is inversely proportional to the area on which the force acts.

questions.q: A wooden block of density 600 kg/m³ is placed in water of density 1000 kg/m³. The block will
options: float with part of it above the water
float completely submerged at any depth
questions.explanation: Its density is less than that of water, so it floats with part above the surface.

questions.q: What is buoyancy (upthrust)? On what does it depend?
questions.answer: Buoyancy is the upward force exerted by a liquid or gas on an object immersed in it. It depends on the density of the fluid and on the volume of the fluid displaced by the object.
questions.explanation: By Archimedes' principle the upthrust equals the weight of fluid displaced.

questions.q: Why do tractors and heavy vehicles have wide tyres?
questions.answer: A wide tyre spreads the weight of the vehicle over a large area. Since pressure is force divided by area, the pressure on the ground is smaller, so the vehicle does not sink into soft soil.
keyPoints: Vehicle does not sink in soft ground
questions.explanation: The same weight gives less pressure if the area is greater.

questions.q: In which situation is work done in the scientific sense?
options: A boy stands holding a bag
A man pushes a wall that does not move
A boy pushes a cart and it moves
questions.explanation: Work needs a force that produces a displacement.

questions.q: One kilowatt-hour is equal to
The energy stored in the food we eat is
questions.explanation: Food stores chemical energy released during respiration.

questions.q: If the speed of a moving body is doubled, its kinetic energy becomes
questions.explanation: KE is proportional to v², so doubling v gives four times the energy.

questions.q: The gravitational potential energy of a body of mass m at height h above the ground is
questions.explanation: PE = mgh.

questions.q: A stone falls freely from a height. Just before it hits the ground, compared with its starting position,
options: its potential energy has decreased and its kinetic energy has increased
questions.explanation: Potential energy changes into kinetic energy as the stone falls.

questions.q: Differentiate between kinetic energy and potential energy with one example of each.
questions.answer: Kinetic energy is the energy a body has because of its motion, for example a moving car. Potential energy is the energy a body has because of its position or state, for example a stone held at a height or a stretched spring.
keyPoints: PE is due to position or state
questions.explanation: Both are forms of mechanical energy.

questions.q: A boy of mass 50 kg climbs 30 steps, each 20 cm high, in 1 minute. Find the work done and his power. (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.answer: Total height = 30 × 0.2 = 6 m. Work done = mgh = 50 × 10 × 6 = 3000 J. Power = work / time = 3000 / 60 = 50 W.
questions.explanation: The work done against gravity is mgh and power is work per unit time.

questions.q: The number of oscillations per second of a vibrating body is its
questions.explanation: Frequency is the number of complete oscillations per second.

questions.q: The maximum displacement of a vibrating particle from its mean position is called its
questions.explanation: Amplitude is the greatest distance moved from the mean position.

questions.q: The distance between two consecutive compressions of a sound wave is its
questions.explanation: Wavelength is the distance between two consecutive compressions or rarefactions.

questions.q: In a sound wave, the region where particles are crowded together and the pressure is high is called a
questions.explanation: A compression is a high-pressure region.

questions.q: Sound travels fastest through which of these?
questions.explanation: Sound is faster in solids than in liquids and gases, and cannot travel in vacuum.

questions.q: A pendulum completes 20 oscillations in 10 s. Its frequency is
questions.explanation: Frequency = 20 / 10 = 2 oscillations per second = 2 Hz.

questions.q: What does SONAR stand for? State one use.
questions.answer: SONAR stands for Sound Navigation And Ranging. It uses ultrasonic waves to find the depth of the sea or to locate objects such as submarines and shoals of fish under water.
keyPoints: Finds depth or locates objects under water
questions.explanation: The time taken by the echo gives the distance.

questions.q: A sound wave has a frequency of 2 kHz and a wavelength of 40 cm. How long will it take to travel 1.5 km?
questions.answer: Speed v = f × λ = 2000 × 0.4 = 800 m/s. Time = distance / speed = 1500 / 800 = 1.875 s.
questions.explanation: Convert kHz to Hz and cm to m before using v = fλ.

questions.q: The removal of unwanted plants from a crop field is called
questions.explanation: Weeds compete with the crop for nutrients, water and light.

questions.q: Which food group gives us most of our carbohydrates for energy?
questions.explanation: Wheat, rice and maize are cereals rich in carbohydrates.

questions.q: Pulses are important in our diet mainly as a source of
questions.explanation: Pulses such as gram and lentil provide protein.

questions.q: Mustard and groundnut are grown mainly to obtain
questions.explanation: Oilseeds supply edible oils, which are rich in fats.

questions.q: Growing two or more crops together in the same field without any definite pattern is called
questions.explanation: In mixed cropping the seeds are mixed and sown together.

questions.q: Why is vermicompost good for the soil?
options: It reduces the water-holding capacity of soil
It improves the fertility and structure of the soil
questions.explanation: Vermicompost is organic, adds nutrients and humus and improves soil structure.

questions.q: Name two sources of water used for irrigation in India.
questions.answer: Common sources of irrigation include wells, canals, river lift systems and tanks.
questions.explanation: The choice depends on the region and the availability of water.

questions.q: Why should a farmer not depend on chemical fertilisers alone year after year?
questions.answer: Continued use of chemical fertilisers alone reduces the organic matter and microorganisms in the soil and damages its structure and fertility. They can also pollute water through run-off. Adding manure or compost along with fertilisers keeps the soil healthy.
keyPoints: Reduces soil organic matter and organisms
questions.explanation: Balanced use of organic and inorganic inputs is better for the soil.
